sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Bochum's parking policy has worked mainly through prices and permits. Resident permits came first: the city proposed in April 2023 to raise the annual permit from €22 to €120, the first rise in over 20 years, across 13 resident zones [7]. The council settled on €90 from 2025, applying to new applications and renewals [8]. A broader parking concept for the inner city followed. Three new resident areas were proposed and five existing ones enlarged, with signage planned for summer 2026 [9][10][11]. A spring 2023 survey found 77% of public street spaces occupied at 5:00 and 84% at 10:00 [11].

The centre itself has been closed to through traffic in places. A 2021 inner-city traffic concept proposed a Südring cycle lane and closing Hans-Böckler-Straße and Viktoriastraße to through traffic around Husemannplatz [12], and by November 2022 a no-through-traffic zone was in place there, although many vehicles still drove through [13]. We found no sourced figures on a low-emission zone or on on-street fee changes, so we do not describe them.

The municipal garages have become more expensive too. From 1 July 2026 the hourly rate rose from €1.60 to €1.90 and the day ticket from €14.40 to €17.10, the first rise since October 2022. BoWE, the city's economic-development company, cited higher personnel, construction, security and cleaning costs and said Bochum remains below neighbouring cities [15].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The big change in supply came in autumn 2023, when BoWE opened two garages in the centre: Husemann Karree (over 500 spaces) and P7 Kurt-Schumacher-Platz (about 430, near the main station), together about 1,000 extra spaces [1][2]. They are filling slowly. Husemann Karree averaged 22% occupancy in 2024 and 34% in 2025, and P7 14% and 21%; in 2026 so far they stand at 34% and 23%. These are means over all hours of the day. The older P1 Husemannplatz reopened fully modernised in October 2022 with 475 spaces [0], then, from March 2024, was to have only 200 of its 477 spaces until mid-July while its stairwells were rebuilt [4]. P8 at Bermuda3Eck had about 100 of its 543 spaces closed for concrete repairs from March 2025 [17].

Other changes have been technical. BoWE rolled out licence-plate payment with EasyPark in eleven garages in August 2024 [5], and the Castroper Straße car park went barrier-free in April 2025 [16]. Charging points in the garages rose from 92 in February 2024 to nearly 100 in September 2026 [3][19]. A discount scheme gives one free hour for purchases of €25 or more in the participating garages [6]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to out-of-town shopping centres, and none on park-and-ride. Ruhr University's own car parks are free and open all day, with part of its central garage closed for renovation until spring 2028 [21].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
All twelve garages in our Bochum data, 6,542 spaces in total, are listed under one brand, Parken in Bochum, and BoWE's announcements name eleven of them. Nine are within 500 m of Husemannplatz (3,797 spaces), and one, the 2,000-space Stadionring garage, is 1.9 km out. Our data lists no private operator, and we found no sourced information on any. Ten of the twelve charge the same, €1.90 an hour and €17.10 a day, so price cannot explain differences among them. P9 Schauspielhaus, the busiest, is one of two that list only a €6 day rate.

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 34% on weekdays and 27% at weekends. Within 500 m of Husemannplatz, weekday occupancy averages 29%, against 46% for the two garages 500 m to 1 km out. P3 at the town hall (20%), Bochumer Fenster (23%), P1 Husemannplatz (24%) and the 700-space P5 Brückstraße (26%) are the emptiest. The fullest is P9 Schauspielhaus (58% on weekdays and 50% at weekends), the only garage above 40% at weekends. The main-station garage P6 and the Stadionring garage follow at 40%, and Husemann Karree at 39%. P5 at 11% and P3 at 6% on weekends show how weekday-driven demand is.

The data cover the summer holidays and the university break, so term-time figures may differ. In the nine garages with data in both years, occupancy averaged 32% in 2022 and 35% in 2025.
